content: Fish cannot leave deep waters, and a country's weapons should not be displayed.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching, Book of Virtue
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. We spend enormous energy trying to present a sanitized, perfect version of ourselves to the world. But whatever emotions or desires we push into the dark don't disappear; they run our lives from behind the curtain.

In Lao Tzu's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. True maturity isn't pretending you have no dark corners—it is having the honesty and courage to look at your jealousy, fear, and anger in the daylight so they no longer control your actions.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
